pride_data.title: Mitochondrial translocase blocking ATP5MG-tFT fusion protein interactome in human embryonic kidney (HEK) 293 cells
pride_data.projectDescription: The experiment uses HEK-293 Flp-In T-Rex cells to express fusion protein that combines ATP synthase subunit ATP5MG with a tandem fluorescent protein timer (tFT). The tFT tag combines mCherry and super folder GFP (sfGFP) fluorescent proteins. An exceptionally stable structure of sfGFP interferes with its import into mitochondria. Thus, ATP5MG-tFT fusion stalls during translocation into mitochondria. We identify the proteome of cells after 24 hours of fusion protein expression. As a control, we use cells that express tFT fusion not directed to mitochondria (ILE-Deg-tFT) or cells that did not express fusion protein. Next, we use chemical crosslinking and GFP-Trap-based immunoprecipitation to define interaction partner proteins of ATP5MG-tFT and ILE-Deg-tFT fusions.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: HEK-293 Flp-In T-Rex cells and their derivatives expressing ATP5MG-tFT or ILE-Deg-tFT were grown in high glucose DMEM medium supplemented with 10% FBS and Penicillin/Streptomycin mix. During the final 24 hours, growth media was supplemented with 1 µg/ml of tetracycline to induce fusion protein synthesis. Cells were harvested in PBS. Pellets of five million cells were crosslinked by incubation in 0,5 ml of 0,5% formaldehyde in PBS for 30 min at room temperature (RT). Next, cell pellets were incubated with 1,25 M glycine solution in PBS for 10 minutes at RT to quench any remaining formaldehyde. After glycine treatment, cells were washed three times with PBS. Three million cells were lysed in 200 µL of lysis buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, 0.5% NP-40, protease inhibitor cocktail) and incubated on ice for 30 min. The lysates were spun at 20,000 g for 10 min to eliminate insoluble material, and protein concentration in the supernatants was measured. Samples were diluted with wash buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH=7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, protease inhibitor cocktail) to adjust protein concentration to 0,3 µg/µg and reduce detergent concentration by approximately three-fold. An equal amount of protein (150 µg) for each sample was used for immunoprecipitation with 10 µL of GFP-Trap Agarose beads slurry (ChromoTek) (supplemented with 40 µL of empty agarose beads to facilitate handling), while 15 µg of each sample was saved and processed as INPUT fractions. The beads were washed with the wash buffer three times and then incubated with trypsin (sequencing grade from Promega, 1 µg) in 50 mM Tris-HCL buffer pH 8.2 containing 5 mM TCEP and 10 mM iodoacetamide overnight at 37 °C. Proteins in the INPUT fractions were subjected to chloroform/methanol precipitation. Protein pellets were resuspended in 50 mM Tris-HCL buffer pH 8.2 containing 5 mM TCEP, 10 mM iodoacetamide. Trypsin (sequencing grade from Promega, 0,5 µg) was added, and the samples were incubated overnight at 37 °C. Proteolysis reactions were quenched by the addition of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA, to the final conc. 1%), and the samples were centrifuged at 12,000 x g for 3 min at RT, to pellet undigested proteins. Tryptic peptides were desalted with the use of AttractSPE™ Disks Bio C18 (Affinisep). Prior to LC-MS measurement, the peptide fractions were resuspended in 0.1% TFA, 2% acetonitrile in water. Chromatographic separation was performed on an Easy-Spray Acclaim PepMap column 50 cm × 75 µm inner diameter (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 45 °C by applying a 135 min acetonitrile gradients in 0.1% aqueous formic acid at a flow rate of 300 nl/min. An UltiMate 3000 nano-LC system was coupled to a Q Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer via an easy-spray source (all Thermo Fisher Scientific). The Q Exactive HF-X was operated in data-dependent mode with survey scans acquired at a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200. Up to 12 of the most abundant isotope patterns with charges z=2-6 from the survey scan were selected with an isolation window of 1.3 m/z and fragmented by higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy of 27, while the dynamic exclusion was set to 30 s. The maximum ion injection times for the survey scan and the MS/MS scans (acquired with a resolution of 15,000 at m/z 200) were 45 and 22 ms, respectively. The ion target value for MS was set to 3e6 and for MS/MS to 1e5, and the intensity threshold for MS/MS was set to 8e2.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The obtained data were processed with MaxQuant v. 1.6.7, and the peptides were identified from the MS/MS spectra searched against Human Reference Proteome UP000005640 using the built-in Andromeda search engine. Raw files corresponding to 12 affinity purified samples (3 conditions, 4 replicates) and 12 INPUT samples (3 conditions, 4 replicates) were loaded into MaxQuant and processed. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification and methionine oxidation as well as protein N-terminal acetylation, were set as variable modifications. For in silico digests of the reference proteome, cleavages of arginine or lysine followed by any amino acid were allowed (trypsin/P), and up to two missed cleavages were allowed. The False Discovery Rate (FDR) was set to 0.01 for peptides, proteins, and sites. Match between runs and LFQ quantification were enabled. Other parameters were used as pre-set in the software. Unique and razor peptides were used for quantification enabling protein grouping (razor peptides are the peptides uniquely assigned to protein groups and not to individual proteins).
